sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the centre of Beverly east of Broad Street, around the junction known as Five Points where East Warren Street, Cooper Street and Bridge Street meet. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The top half shows blocks 47, 48 and 52 between East 2nd Street and East 3rd Street and north of East Warren Street, bounded by Laurel Street on the west, Cooper and Walnut Streets in the middle and Vankirk Street on the east; Freeman Lane crosses the upper right. Most of these lots hold frame dwellings, with the Worth Motor Car Company garage and auto sales building (concrete block, with a 30-car garage) and American Legion Post 115 along Cooper Street. Below Five Points the plan changes to a fan of diagonal streets: Cooper Street runs south-east toward Church Street, Bridge Street south-west toward East Oak, and Perkins and Elizabeth Streets cross between them, giving the wedge-shaped blocks 55, 56, 58 and 59. Commercial buildings cluster here, among them the First National Bank, printing shops, a bakery, a movie house with a store block at East Warren and Bridge, and the post office with an auditorium and club rooms above. A cemetery occupies the lower left between Bridge Street and East Oak. Water pipes of 4 to 10 inches are lettered along the streets and street widths of 25 to 60 feet are given. Neighbouring sheets are indicated by their numbers: 4 above, 5 to the left, 10 to the right and 6 below.
notes: Vankirk is Van Kirk Street, Freeman Lane is Freemans Lane and Willmerton (with Wilmerton in brackets) is Wilmerton Street in OpenStreetMap; East Warren, East Oak, East 2nd and East 3rd are Warren Street, Oak Street, 2nd Street and 3rd Street.
Cooper Street / Oak Street was rejected at 7.4 m: the modern Oak Street line near Cooper does not follow the drawn one.
Bridge, Perkins and Willmerton were not used as control (diagonal streets).
50 ft. Centre of Beverly east of Broad: Five Points, Cooper, Walnut, Warren, Church, Oak; Cooper/Oak rejected (7.4 m).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the Delaware riverfront of old Beverly west of Broad Street, at 50 feet to an inch. The Delaware River crosses the top of the sheet in blue, with a stepped shoreline in the upper right and the line of West Bank Street running along the water. Most of the western half is open ground within blocks 2, 3 and 7, marked only by dashed block lines and a few outbuildings; the Sewerage Pump House stands near the shore and Beverly School No. 2 (Colored), a brick building with class rooms and a corridor, stands lower left. The built-up part lies on the right, between Magnolia Street, Locust Street and Broad Street, in blocks 8, 9, 10 and 11. Frame dwellings of one to two and a half storeys line the streets in regular narrow lots on either side of West Front Street, with a lumber storage yard on block 9 and, on block 11, a bakery with oven and a small group of stores and dwellings facing Broad Street. Penn Street runs across the upper part and West 2nd Street along the bottom; water pipes of 4 to 16 inches are lettered, including a suction pipe and 16 inch main near Broad Street. Street widths of 30 to 80 feet are lettered. The sheet carries a compass rose; the blocks continue on sheet 4 to the right and on sheet 5 below.
notes: Bank Street is Bank Road in OpenStreetMap; West Front, West 2nd and Penn are Front Street, 2nd Street and Penn Street.
Broad Street / Front Street was not detected (pipes and the sheet edge); Penn Street is drawn about 39 feet wide against 59 feet in the parcels.
50 ft. Delaware riverfront west of Broad: Bank, Penn, Front, 2nd, Magnolia, Locust; mostly open ground; Penn drawn about 39 ft against 59 ft parcels.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the Beverly riverfront east of Broad Street, at 50 feet to an inch, from Broad Street on the left to Walnut Street on the right, with the Delaware River crossing the upper right in blue. Broad Street, labelled with a width of 60 to 80 feet, runs down the left edge; the stepped shoreline of sheet 3 continues at the top left. East Bank Street runs diagonally along the water, between a stone wall and blocks 39, 40, 41 and 42, most of which are open. On block 40 the Delaware Water Company works stand beside Broad Street: a large vacant sawtooth-roofed concrete-floored building not in operation, an electric pump house, offices and the company's plant in operation all hours. Further along the shore on block 45 a coal yard, not in operation, with coal sheds, a boat house and lime and other storage, occupies the point between the stone walls. South of East Front Street the blocks are built up with frame dwellings, a boat shop, small stables and Grace Chapel (Presbyterian) on block 43, between Broad and Laurel Streets, and further blocks 44 and 45 east of Laurel Street. East 2nd Street runs along the bottom. Water pipes of 4 to 16 inches are lettered, and a 16 inch suction pipe runs at the top left. Sheet 3 joins on the left, sheet 5 below and sheet 2 below right.
notes: West and East Bank are Bank Road in OpenStreetMap; East Front and East 2nd are Front Street and 2nd Street.
Penn Street is drawn about 39 feet wide against 59 feet in the parcels; its junction with Broad Street was kept, with 1.7 m residual.
50 ft. Riverfront east of Broad: E. Bank, Front, 2nd, Laurel, Cooper, Walnut, Delaware Water Co.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the centre of old Beverly between West and East 2nd Street at the top and West and East Oak Street at the bottom, and from the open ground west of Magnolia Street across Locust and Broad Streets to Laurel Street on the east. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and shows blocks 13 to 18, 23, 24, 46, 50 and 53. The blocks along Locust and Broad Streets are built up with frame dwellings, many of them two-storey, with stores on Broad Street near 2nd Street, while the western blocks toward Bently Avenue are largely open lots with scattered houses. Warren Street crosses the lower part of the sheet on a diagonal, and the block corner at Broad and East Warren holds a garage with a sales room and a concrete-block show room and paint shop. Institutions are prominent: St. Joseph's Home for the Aged with its laundry and dormitory building at the west edge, the Macedonian (Colored) Baptist Church on block 14, St. James Baptist Church (Colored) on Locust Street, the Beverly Baptist Church on block 24, St. Joseph's Catholic Church with its rectory and a concrete-block auditorium and recreation hall on block 23, and on block 53 the Hope Hose Company No. 2 fire house combined with a public school. Water pipes of 4 to 12 inches are drawn along the streets, and street widths of 30 to 80 feet are lettered; Broad Street is 80 feet wide. A filling station stands at the corner of Magnolia and West Warren. The sheet joins sheets 3 and 4 to the north, 2 to the east, 6 and 9 to the south and 9 to the west.
notes: Bently Avenue is Bentley Avenue in OpenStreetMap; its junction with Warren Street lies at the sheet edge and was left out (2.7 m residual, raised the fit error).
Warren, 2nd, 3rd and Oak are printed with West and East prefixes; OpenStreetMap uses Warren Street, 2nd Street, 3rd Street and Oak Street.
50 ft. Centre of old Beverly: W./E. 2nd, 3rd, Warren, Oak; Magnolia, Locust, Broad, Laurel. Pilot sheet: 16 automatic points, ink_below_paper 80.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the blocks of Beverly between East Oak Street and East Pine Street east of Broad Street, at 50 feet to an inch. On the left, Broad Street and Laurel Street frame blocks 61 and 69; block 61 carries the Beverly City Public High School No. 1, a large brick and pink-coloured building with kitchen box, and a row of dwellings beneath it, and block 69 holds frame dwellings, a carpenter and auto shop and a wagon shed with autos on East Pine. In the middle, Bridge Street runs diagonally between East Oak and East Putnam, past the Fire Department, Beverly Fire Company No. 1 building on the upper left and the Auditorium Lodge Hall on block 63. East Putnam Street runs across the sheet at a slant to Spruce Street, and blocks 70 and 71 below it are filled with frame dwellings, a printing shop and small storehouses. On the right Cooper Street and East Oak enclose block 64, where a garage with a 15-car capacity and a long blue-coloured storage building stand at the Oak Street end, and Chestnut Street runs diagonally down to East Pine. Block 2 above and block 7 below, and sheets 5, 9 and 10, are named in the margins. Street widths of 25 to 80 feet and 4 to 8 inch water pipes are lettered.
notes: East Oak, East Putnam and East Pine are Oak Street, Putnam Street and Pine Street in OpenStreetMap.
Bridge, Cooper, Chestnut and the diagonal ends of Oak and Putnam were not used as control.
50 ft. Oak to Pine east of Broad: Beverly City Public High School No. 1, Bridge, Putnam, Spruce, Chestnut.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the south-eastern part of old Beverly between East Pine Street and the Pennsylvania Railroad, at 50 feet to an inch. Broad Street, Laurel Street and Spruce Street run north to south through blocks 73, 74 and 75, with Chestnut Street cutting the right-hand corner diagonally. The blocks are mostly lined with frame dwellings on long narrow lots, with a few auto repair shops, among them E. F. Woolston's auto repair and body building on East Pine, and a concrete storage building. At the bottom of the blocks East Railroad Avenue runs beside the Beverly Century Corporation, a large knitting, boxing and finishing mill with a sprinkler tank and a descriptive note on its fire protection, and the C. S. Parsons works making pincers, pliers and nippers. The Pennsylvania Railroad (Amboy Division) crosses the sheet diagonally with a line of city limits drawn along it, and a coal yard of A. T. Perkins is shown with a curved siding. South of the tracks stands Robert F. Hobbs Inc., a wall paper manufactory with printing, manufacturing, cutting and colour rooms, a carpenter shop and a roller store, with its own siding. A few dwellings and sheds near Broad Street at the lower left belong to sheet 8. Water pipes of 4 to 6 inches and street widths of 50 to 80 feet are lettered.
notes: East Pine and East Railroad Avenue are Pine Street and Railroad Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Railroad Avenue was used only at Laurel Street, other junctions were not detected.
Only 5 control points (three along Pine Street): the leave-one-out error is not meaningful.
50 ft. Pine to the railroad east of Broad: Beverly Century Corpn, Robt. F. Hobbs wall paper works; south half placed by one hand-picked rail crossing (S. Broad St).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 shows the Wall Rope Works south of the Pennsylvania Railroad's Amboy Division, between Mount Holly Road on the west and South Broad Street or Bridgeboro Road on the east, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Along the top the sheet repeats the south edge of sheet 9: West Railroad Avenue with the ends of Melbourne Street, Bently Avenue and Locust Street, then the railroad tracks, with the city limits running along them. The rope works fill the upper left of the sheet: long fibre storage buildings with shipping platforms and a covered wooden platform along the railroad, frame storage and rope buildings on brick piers, and a brick and fireproof core of preparation, spinning and rope machine rooms, a cable house, an engine room, a machine shop, an oakum room, offices, oil tanks, a 100,000 gallon cistern, a 100,000 gallon tank on a steel truss and a 35,000 gallon service and sprinkler tank. A rope walk runs south for the full height of the sheet along Mount Holly Road. A long block of notes describes the plant's watchmen, sprinklers, water supply and fire hoses. The rest of the sheet is the open Wall Rope Works yard (block 131) and part of block 132, with a few frame dwellings along South Broad Street. Most of the sheet is open ground.
notes: The road on the east is lettered 'S. Broad St. or Bridgeboro Rd.'; OpenStreetMap names it Bridgeboro Road south of Railroad Avenue.

Placed by a two-point helmert transformation from the railroad crossings of Mount Holly Road (detected) and Bridgeboro Road (hand-picked on the water pipe in South Broad Street at the middle of the tracks); no street junction is drawn in full on the sheet. Low confidence.
Bently Avenue is Bentley Avenue in OpenStreetMap.

50 ft. Wall Rope Works south of the railroad between Mount Holly Rd and S. Broad St or Bridgeboro Rd; no complete street junction; placed by a helmert on two railroad crossings (one hand-picked). Low confidence.

sheet-9-1.description: The main part of sheet 9 covers the western half of Beverly, the district shown on the key map as Beverly Manor, from West 3rd Street at the top down to the Pennsylvania Railroad's Amboy Division and West Railroad Avenue at the bottom, and from Lee Avenue east to Broad Street. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch. West Warren, West Putnam, West Pine and Cherry cross the sheet from west to east, and Lee Avenue, Mount Holly Street, Melbourne, Bently Avenue, Magnolia, Locust and Broad run down it; West Oak enters from the east, and 4th Street ends at the open ground in the north-west. The blocks east of Magnolia (25, 26, 30, 31, 35, 36) are built up with closely set frame dwellings, and Mount Holly Street is lined on both sides with rows of small concrete-block and frame houses. West of Lee Avenue and in the north-west quarter the land is still open, with scattered houses and coops on large blocks numbered 12, 19, 145 and 146; blocks 33, 34, 37 and 38 south of Pine are laid out in lots but largely unbuilt. Named buildings include St. Joseph's Home for the Aged with its dormitory (its report is on sheet 5), the Bethel A.M.E. Church on Magnolia, the City Hall and Public School No. 2 at Broad and Oak, and a gasoline station on West Warren. At the foot of Mount Holly Street by the railroad stand the vacant buildings of the former Beverly Mills, drawn again at a larger scale in the inset at the lower left (part 2). The city limits run along the railroad.
notes: Mount Holly Street north of the railroad is Manor Road in OpenStreetMap; south of it the road is Mount Holly Road. Bently Avenue is Bentley Avenue.
Lee Avenue was left out of the fit: its modern line runs at an angle to the drawn street (junction residuals 5 to 6 m). Railroad Avenue was also left out (residuals 4 to 14 m).
West Pine is offset where it crosses Mount Holly Street; both modern Pine Street / Manor Road nodes, about 32 m apart, match the drawn jog.
4th Street has no modern counterpart in the reference data.

100 ft. Western Beverly (Beverly Manor), W. 3rd to the railroad, Lee Av to Broad; part 1 main map; part 2 inset: enlarged plan (about 50 ft) of the former Beverly Mills at Mount Holly St and the railroad, placed from building corners carried from part 1.

sheet-9-2.description: An inset at the lower left of sheet 9, framed by a heavy line, gives an enlarged plan of the buildings of the former Beverly Mills, which the main part of the sheet draws at small scale at the foot of Mount Holly Street beside the Pennsylvania Railroad. The inset is drawn at twice the scale of the sheet, about 50 feet to an inch, and turned so that north points up and to the right, as its own north arrow shows; it is marked 'For location see below'. Mount Holly Street runs along its right side and the railroad's Amboy Division along its bottom. The plant on block 19 consists of several large concrete-block buildings, a two-storey brick mill range with storage wings and a chimney, a frame office by the street and smaller outbuildings. The notes record no watchman, steam heat, electric light and power, and the hydrants shown; 4 inch water pipes run along the street and the railroad.
notes: No street junction lies in the inset; it was placed from five building corners carried from the same buildings on the main part of the sheet (sheet-9-1), so its placement follows that part. Fitted scale 7.71 px/ft against 7.9 expected for 50 ft to an inch; low confidence.
The main map letters the plant as vacant.

100 ft. Western Beverly (Beverly Manor), W. 3rd to the railroad, Lee Av to Broad; part 1 main map; part 2 inset: enlarged plan (about 50 ft) of the former Beverly Mills at Mount Holly St and the railroad, placed from building corners carried from part 1.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 shows eastern Beverly from the Delaware River to the Pennsylvania Railroad, at 100 feet to an inch. The river crosses the top; Riverbank Road runs along the shore with scattered boat houses and club houses, and Vankirk Street, Vansciver Street and Farnum Lane run inland from it. East Warren Street crosses the sheet from the Willmerton junction on the left to Farnum Street on the right and is lined with frame dwellings; the Beverly M. E. Church and St. Stephens Episcopal Church with its parish house and rectory are on blocks 67 and 57. Perkins and Church Streets run east to west across blocks 60, 78, 79, 80 and 81, with the Farnum School (public) on block 80, and Jennings and Parker Streets run between them. The Beverly City and Edgewater Park boundary is drawn along the right side near Farnum Street. In the lower left the street pattern turns to Cooper, Chestnut, Elizabeth, Walton and East Pine Streets, with dense frame housing on blocks 65, 66, 72, 76, 77 and 82, and a finishing works at Garfield Avenue on block 85. East Railroad Avenue runs along the railroad at the bottom beside Beverly Station and the John A. Bidwell Company works making cotton towels. At top left is a corner of sheet 4 with the Rangocas Club on block 49. Sheet numbers 2, 6, 7 and 13 mark the neighbouring sheets.
notes: Vankirk, Vansciver, Willmerton and Freeman Lane are Van Kirk Street, Van Sciver Street, Wilmerton Street and Freemans Lane in OpenStreetMap.
East Warren Street junctions were 4 to 6 m off in the same direction and were left out; the Elizabeth / Jennings / Pine cluster was also left out (7 to 23 m).
The fitted rotation (7.7 degrees) is lower than the 10 degrees of the 50 ft sheets; confidence is low to medium.

100 ft. Eastern Beverly from the river to the railroad around Farnum St; one part; Warren Street and the Elizabeth/Jennings/Pine cluster left out as displaced; fitted rotation 7.7 degrees against about 10 elsewhere.

sheet-11-1.description: The main part of sheet 11 covers the western end of Edgewater Park, east of Beverly, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned on the page: north points to the left, toward the Delaware River, which runs down the left side of this part, and the Pennsylvania Railroad's Amboy Division runs down the right edge. East Warren crosses the part on a long diagonal from Farnum Lane at the bottom toward sheet 12 at the top, with house numbers along both sides. Below it, Farnum Lane and Farnum Street form the boundary with Beverly (sheet 10), and King Road, Church and the end of East Church Street and East Pine Street meet them. Franklin and Anderson Avenue (marked not opened and arbitrary) branch off East Warren toward the railroad. The land is divided into large blocks, numbered 101 to 103 and 108 to 111, most of them river-front estates and open land: large frame and brick dwellings with greenhouses, servants' houses and a well house stand on deep lots between the river and East Warren, and a stone dwelling stands on block 110. Smaller houses are grouped at the bottom near Farnum Lane, King Road and Church, where block 101 holds the Beverly Presbyterian Church. The strip at the left edge, behind a heavy line, is a separate part of the sheet (part 2, Wood Lane), drawn at another angle.
notes: East Warren is Warren Street East in OpenStreetMap; Franklin is Keim Street; Church is Church Street East; King Road is King Street.
Anderson Avenue is lettered as not opened and arbitrary.

Placed from four detected junctions only (Warren Street East and Church Street East with Farnum Street and with Keim Street); a hand-picked King Road / Farnum Lane point disagreed with them by several metres and was dropped, and Farnum / Pine at the bottom edge was not detected.

100 ft, turned (north to the left). Part 1: western Edgewater Park, E. Warren, Franklin (now Keim St), Church, Farnum Lane; part 2: strip along Wood Lane south of the railroad behind a heavy line, drawn at another angle (north up-right), anchored on the Woodlane Road rail crossing. Low confidence for both.

sheet-11-2.description: The left strip of sheet 11, enclosed by a heavy line, shows Wood Lane where it runs south from the Pennsylvania Railroad at the eastern edge of Edgewater Park, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north pointing up and to the right, as its own north arrow shows. The railroad crosses the top of the strip, and Wood Lane runs straight down the strip below it with house numbers on both sides. The land on either side is in large blocks, numbered 122, 123 and 136, and is farmland with scattered buildings: frame dwellings, a few brick ones, corn cribs, a wagon shed, coops, sheds and an ice house. The heavy boundary line steps in and out to take in the farm buildings set back from the lane. The rest of the sheet (part 1) shows the western end of Edgewater Park at a different angle.
notes: Wood Lane is Woodlane Road in OpenStreetMap.

Placed from a single point, the Woodlane Road crossing of the River Line, with an assumed scale (3.82 px/ft from part 1) and rotation from the measured lines (20 degrees, against about 18 degrees from the modern bearing of Woodlane Road); low confidence.

100 ft, turned (north to the left). Part 1: western Edgewater Park, E. Warren, Franklin (now Keim St), Church, Farnum Lane; part 2: strip along Wood Lane south of the railroad behind a heavy line, drawn at another angle (north up-right), anchored on the Woodlane Road rail crossing. Low confidence for both.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 shows the eastern part of Edgewater Park along the Delaware River, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Like sheet 11 it is turned on the page, with north pointing to the left, so the river runs down the left side and the Pennsylvania Railroad's Amboy Division down the right. Park Avenue runs across the top of the sheet and Edgewater Avenue, Cliff Avenue and Wood Avenue (continuing as Wood Lane beyond the railroad) run parallel to it lower down, crossed by Linden Avenue, Cottage Avenue and Summer Avenue; East Warren enters at the lower right and Burlington Avenue runs beside the railroad at the right edge. The district is a suburb of large lots: frame dwellings, many of two and a half storeys, with a few brick and concrete-block houses, greenhouses, coops and a lodge, on blocks numbered 103 to 107 and 111 to 118, and the large river-front block 104 holds only a few big houses. By the railroad stand the Edgewater Park station, a post office and store at East Warren, and the yard of Hugh B. Miller, building and contracting, east of the tracks, where stone retaining walls line the cut. The top edge and the lower right corner are marked 'no exposure', and the strip below Wood Avenue shows parts of blocks 103, 111 and 122 with a few buildings.
notes: Wood Avenue and Wood Lane are Woodlane Road in OpenStreetMap; East Warren is Warren Street East, which today also follows the line of Burlington Avenue beyond the railroad.

The sheet is drawn about 7 percent smaller than its nominal 100 ft to an inch (fitted 3.68 px/ft against about 3.95 on the other 100 ft sheets), and its fit leaves residuals of 3 to 7 m at some junctions; medium confidence.
The East Warren / Wood Avenue junction (about 8 m off, modern line realigned) and a false Edgewater Avenue / Warren Street East match beyond the railroad were excluded.
100 ft, turned (north to the left). Eastern Edgewater Park: Park, Edgewater, Cliff, Wood Avs; Linden, Cottage, Summer Avs; drawn about 7 percent small.

sheet-13-1.description: The main part of sheet 13 shows South Beverly, the settlement south of the Pennsylvania Railroad's Amboy Division, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Along the top runs East Railroad Avenue beside the double-track line, with the ends of Chestnut, Cooper and Elizabeth Streets, Walton Avenue, Sassafras Alley and Farnum Street meeting it from the north and the city limits crossing near Farnum Street. South of the tracks, near the foot of South Cooper Street, stand the P.R.R. freight station with its wooden platform, the storage and office buildings of the Co-operative Growers Association with a loading shed, and L. A. Page's dealership in farmers' supplies. South Cooper Street then runs down the sheet as the spine of a thinly built district of frame dwellings, coops, sheds and small barns on long narrow lots, with Van Rossum crossing at the left edge and Chestnut Avenue, the 100 foot wide Franklin Avenue and two unnamed lanes crossing between them. Blocks 120, 121, 133, 134, 137 and 138 are numbered; much of the east half of the part is open farm land with only a few scattered buildings, among them a cluster of farm buildings reached by a lane off South Cooper Street. A water pipe of 6 inches runs in Franklin Avenue and in South Cooper Street. The lower right corner of the sheet is a separate inset of Perkins (part 2), divided from this part by a heavy line, and the sheet's scale bar and compass rose stand in the open ground beside it.
notes: Franklin Avenue is West Franklin Avenue in OpenStreetMap; its junctions with Cooper Street and Van Rossum Avenue were left out because both sat about 3 m off the fit in the same direction (modern right-of-way centre not on the drawn line).
Chestnut Avenue between Van Rossum and South Cooper is Nicki's Place (east of Van Rossum) and Chestnut Alley in OpenStreetMap; the lane south of Franklin Avenue is Walnut Alley.
Van Rossum is Van Rossum Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The Cooper Street grade crossing of the River Line was detected but rejected (4.2 m off the street fit).

100 ft. Part 1: South Beverly (S. Cooper St, Franklin Av, Van Rossum) south of the railroad; part 2: inset of Perkins behind a heavy line, turned (north up-right), anchored on the Perkins Lane rail crossing; low confidence.

sheet-13-2.description: An inset in the lower right corner of sheet 13, enclosed by a heavy line, shows the hamlet of Perkins west of Beverly, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points about twenty degrees to the right of straight up, as its own north arrow shows. The Pennsylvania Railroad's Amboy Division crosses the top of the inset in a right of way lettered Perkins Street, with a passenger station on its north side and a freight station with a platform on the south side, beside the crossing of Perkins Lane. Perkins Lane runs down the inset from the railroad, a narrow lane with house numbers on both sides. The land on either side is divided into large blocks, numbered 126 to 129, and is thinly built: scattered frame dwellings, coops and sheds on large lots, with a single brick dwelling. The inset's left and right edges are marked as having no exposure. Nothing else in the inset survives as a street junction, so it was placed from the one grade crossing.
notes: Placed from a single point, the Perkins Lane crossing of the River Line (the former P.R.R. Amboy Division), with the scale of part 1 (3.881 px/ft) and rotation from the measured lines (20.6 degrees, against about 21.5 degrees from the modern bearing of Perkins Lane); low confidence.
Perkins Street is the railroad right of way; the street running beside the line today is Railroad Avenue.

100 ft. Part 1: South Beverly (S. Cooper St, Franklin Av, Van Rossum) south of the railroad; part 2: inset of Perkins behind a heavy line, turned (north up-right), anchored on the Perkins Lane rail crossing; low confidence.
